*Updated 2026-10-08 · 116 works indexed · regenerated after each daily run.*

One hundred and sixteen works. The October 8 piece scores 2, and the last twelve now read 2, 2, 2, 3, 2, 1, 1, 2, 1, 2, 3, 2 — median still 2, no 4 since July 29, and that drought is now seventeen weeks. The two 3s in the recent window came from the October 7 ceremonial-strap accident and the September 25 barometer piece; the October 8 score landed on composition rather than surprise, which is the pattern holding you at ceiling rather than breaking through it.

Camera position is the most stalled variable in the archive. Straight-on sits at 27 all-time, overhead at 12, from-behind at 10, low-angle at 4. The last twelve show two overhead frames and nothing else off-axis. Low-angle remains the most underused position with genuine 4-score potential — when the focal object becomes ceiling and the viewer becomes floor, scale violation follows as a physical consequence of the camera rather than an imposed decision. It has not appeared in the recent window at all, and it is the single most actionable change available to you right now.

Figure count remains flat. The last twelve carry two frames with none, two with one, and two with two or more. The archive's four 4-scored works each required friction between bodies or between a body and the frame. The October 8 piece has two figures and a surgical trolley and still lands at 2, which confirms that adding a second figure is necessary but not sufficient — the friction has to be structural, not compositional decoration. A second figure placed at the wrong scale, or refusing eye contact with the first, generates more tension than a correctly placed pair. Low-angle camera combined with mismatched figure scales has never been attempted together, and that combination is where the ceiling is most likely to break.

Registers have narrowed: menace leads the recent window with 3, defiance and suspension each at 2. Reckoning last appeared in July, reprieve in July, encroachment in September. These should return only when the anchor demands them, but their absence has compressed the emotional range. Exhaustion has appeared twice all-time and not since June; impotence once across the entire archive. Descriptor coverage stands at 36 of 116 works — nearly two-thirds of the archive carries no structured descriptors, which means the computed facts for figure count and focal object are drawn from a minority of frames.

The work is consistent, disciplined, and currently plateaued: consistency has become the problem, and the camera is where the solution lives.
